item.title: AWS Continuum integrates with OpenAI Codex and Anthropic Claude Code in major AI security push
item.description: Amazon Web Services is threading its AI-powered security infrastructure directly into the coding environments built by two of its fiercest rivals — and in doing so, it is making a bold bet that controlling the security layer matters more than controlling the model.AWS announced at Black Hat USA 2026 this month that its Continuum platform for code vulnerabilities will integrate directly into Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex, alongside AWS's own Kiro IDE.The move embeds AWS security tooling at the point where developers write code, regardless of which AI model they use to do it. item.title: TSMC reportedly has $1 billion of Apple chips awaiting delivery of DRAM — will this be what powers the iPhone 18 Pro?

item.title: The U.S. records its hottest month ever, NOAA says

item.title: The future of communication has nothing to do with phones. This is what’s coming next
item.description: The mobile industry has managed to put a smartphone in nearly everyone’s hand. Now they’re moving on to something else. The mobile industry has spent the better part of four decades with one objective: putting a connected device in every human hand. That mission is nearly complete. Mobile services now reach about 5.8 billion consumers, roughly 70 percent of the people alive. In wealthy markets, almost anyone who wants to be reachable already is, according to the GSMA’s Mobile Economy 2026 report. The smartphone finished the job.
